To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the trypanosome transcriptome is regulated in a highly coordinated fashion, and that this regulation occurs at the level of mRNA decay, which is controlled by the cell cycle, the metabolic status of the cell and the environment.
trypanosome gene expression forms regulons in which co-regulation is observed at the level of mRNA degradation.

the trypanosome transcriptome is regulated in a highly co-regulated manner, that mRNAs encoding proteins with functions in particular metabolic pathways, or encoding proteins in the same complexes are co-regulated, and that mRNAs that show similar regulation patterns are likely to be regulated by the same factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression during differentiation.

how the transcriptome is regulated during the differentiation of bloodstream trypanosomes to procyclic forms, which occurs when they are transferred from the bloodstream of the mammalian host to the midguts of the Tsetse fly.
the regulation of gene expression and the mechanisms of differentiation in trypanosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trypanosome transcriptome is highly dynamic, with the regulation of mRNA abundance being a key feature of differentiation and adaptation.
trypanosome genes form regulons in which co-regulated mRNAs with common functional characteristics show identical or very similar patterns of regulation.
the post-transcription regulation of gene expression during differentiation of bloodstream forms into procyclic forms is complex and involves many mRNAs and proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trypanosomes use mRNA degradation as the main regulatory mechanism, but that the degradation of mRNAs encoding proteins with different functions is coordinated.

, in addition to the well-known regulation of gene expression by RNA binding proteins, trypanosomes use the same proteins to control the expression of many different genes, and that this regulation is mediated by the cell cycle and/or the cell cycle checkpoint.

trypanosome mRNA regulation is a complex system, in which many genes are co-regulated in response to environmental changes, but with a large number of genes that are regulated in response to other signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trypanosomes use a sophisticated system of post-transcriptional regulation, which allows them to respond rapidly to environmental changes.
post-transcriptional regulation is a powerful mechanism to coordinate expression of genes involved in different pathways.
the transcriptome is organized into regulons of mRNAs with similar functions.
